newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil slow, but firm with no signs weakness.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil slow, but firm with no signs weakness.

text.p: Low and high sulphur cracked fuel were firmer on Monday deriving support from tight supplies and bouyant crude that broke the $24 a barrel barrier.

High sulphur barges bounced higher with trades opening around $118 fob ARA and done at $120 fob ARA towards the end of the day. "It's been an active an active day on the barges with a lot of deals p and c," said one dealer, who added that bunker demand was slow.
High sulphur cargoes were also assessed firm with a major looking to cover a short into the U.K. at around $123 cif NWE, although some were cautious about this price.
"That's a very big number, although I'd agree they would have to pay over $120 cif," said one trader.
News that Romania is looking to buy 500,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel ahead of winter gave support. The country is looking to import four million tonnes of fuel oil annually.

Low sulphur cargoes were a touch stronger in slow physical trade and tight supplies. "Last week people were battering my door to buy, but there's been no-one today," said one seller with a mid month cargo. Low sulphur's strength was derived from crude. "It's got no life of its own," one dealer said. Prices were assessed close to swaps, around $126-127 fob NWE.
